top.openFilesHint: Loads all the files of a .nfs file.
top.openAppHint: Loads a .nwa file (you can also drop it on the page).

top.reloadHint: A file given to the server changed on disk: reload it.
top.stepHint: Advances one frame (while paused): the application runs to the end of the next frame and is given 1/60 s.

watch.title: Watchpoints
watch.help: A watchpoint records the application's accesses to a memory range and tells which instruction makes them: find the address of a score with the value search, watch it for writes, and you will know which instruction changes it. Click an instruction's address to see it in the editor. Watching slows the emulation down.
watch.stopHint: Pauses the application right after the first access.
watch.invalid: Invalid address or number of bytes.

debug.noApp: Load an application to debug it.
debug.stepHint: Runs a single instruction, then stops.
debug.overHint: Like “Step”, but a function call (bl, blx) runs to its end.
debug.followHint: Goes back to the current instruction.
debug.stackHelp: Estimated from the return addresses found on the stack: an old address left on the stack may slip in. Click a line to see the call.
debug.stackRunning: Pause to see the call stack.
debug.registersHelp: Enter applies a change (decimal or 0x…). Registers that just changed are orange.
debug.breakpointsHelp: Click the dot left of an instruction to set or remove a breakpoint. Execution is slower while any exists.

mini.label: Simulation information
mini.openPanel: Open the tools panel: files, memory, structures, keys, settings, trace
mini.statusHint: Whether the simulation is running, paused, or the app has ended or crashed.
mini.framesHint: Number of screen frames drawn since launch (60 per second on the calculator).
mini.timeHint: How long the application has been running. It stops while the simulation is paused.
mini.speedHint: Frequency of the emulated processor. Set it in the Settings tab.
mini.faultHint: The application did something illegal (invalid memory access, unknown instruction…) and stopped.
mini.captureHint: Saves the screen as a PNG image.
mini.copyHint: Copies the screen to the clipboard, ready to paste into a message or document.
mini.recordHint: Records the screen as an animated image until the next click.
mini.recordStopHint: Ends the recording and downloads the GIF.
mini.fullscreenHint: Shows only the screen, without the keys. Space or Escape to exit.
mini.largeHint: Enlarges the screen within the page, without the calculator keys. It adapts to the panel open beside it.
mini.rateHint: Millions of emulated processor instructions executed per real second, measured over the last half second.
mini.slowHint: The application asks for more instructions than this computer can emulate within the real time of a frame: it runs slower than on the real calculator. The “unlimited” mode (Settings) does not change this: it only lets the emulation go as fast as it can.

panel.label: Tools panel
panel.resizeHint: Drag to resize (or use the left and right arrows).

files.storageHint: Space used in the memory that holds the calculator's scripts and settings.
files.corrupt: The file system is damaged at byte {offset} (by the app?).
files.importNfsHint: Loads all the files of a .nfs file.

{name}: replace all the calculator's files with those of the file?

files.exportNfsHint: Saves all the calculator's files into a .nfs file.
files.hint: Right-click (or Menu key) to rename, copy the size, download or delete. F2 renames, Delete deletes (Shift + Delete: no confirmation). Ctrl + click or Shift + click to select several.
files.confirmDeleteMany: Delete these {n} files? This cannot be undone.
files.clearAllHint: Deletes all the calculator's files (after confirmation).
files.confirmClear: Delete all {n} of the calculator's files? This cannot be undone.

state.title: Emulation state
state.help: Saves the app, memory, files and registers in a .nds file so you can resume later, exactly at the same point.
state.saveHint: Saves the state to a .nds file.

memory.heapHint: Memory the application requests as it goes (malloc). The bar shows the highest point reached.
memory.stackHint: Memory for function calls and local variables. The bar shows the deepest point reached.

memmap.label: Memory map
memmap.markerHint: {name} at {address}: see in the Structures tab
memmap.simulatedWhole: {name}: the calculator's system does not exist here, the emulator plays its role.
memmap.note: Real: what the application sees as on a real calculator (its code, RAM, files). Simulated: what the emulator fabricates in place of the system (headers, kernel RAM…). Click an area to view it in hex.
memmap.clickHint: Click to see it in hexadecimal.

explain.system: Headers and tables the calculator's system leaves in memory; here the emulator makes them up.
explain.appsflash: Part of the flash memory reserved for external applications.
explain.files: The calculator's storage: scripts and settings.
explain.app: The application's code, as loaded in flash memory.
explain.data: The application's variables (initialized and uninitialized data).
explain.heap: The heap: memory the application requests while running.
explain.stack: The stack: local variables and return addresses of functions.
explain.reserved: Entirely simulated area: the calculator's system does not exist here.
explain.region: An area of the processor's memory map.

hex.label: Hex editor
hex.watchHint: Sets a watchpoint on the selection: you will see which instructions write it (see Watchpoints).
hex.fillValue: Fill {count} byte(s) with the hexadecimal value (one byte, 00 to ff):
hex.inspector: Values of the selected byte or range
hex.pauseToEdit: Pause the simulation to edit memory.
hex.unmapped: {address} is not in any memory region.
hex.badByte: Invalid value: one or two hexadecimal digits are expected (examples: 00, 7f, 0xff).
hex.badPattern: Invalid pattern: hexadecimal bytes (de ad be ef) or quoted text.
hex.help: Memory is shown in real time and can be edited live, whether the application is running or paused. Click or arrows to move, Shift to select. In the hex column, two digits change a byte; in the ASCII column, each typed character replaces the byte under the cursor. Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+V pastes bytes. Orange bytes just changed.
hex.badChar: “{char}” does not fit in one byte: only characters with code 0 to 255 can be written.
hex.selected: no byte selected | 1 byte selected | {n} bytes selected
hex.inspectNone: Select a byte (or a range) to see its values.
hex.valueFill: Fills the selected byte from {address}, repeating the value | Fills the selected byte from {address}, repeating the value | Fills the {n} selected bytes from {address}, repeating the value
hex.valueEdit: Writes from {address} (first selected byte) | Writes 1 byte from {address} (first selected byte) | Writes {n} bytes from {address} (first selected byte)
hex.valueBadDec: Invalid decimal value for this type ({type}).
hex.valueBadHex: Invalid hexadecimal value: at most as many digits as the type has bytes ({type}).
hex.clickToEdit: Click to edit this value from the first selected byte

structures.invalid: Invalid: the structure does not look as expected (overwritten by the app?).
structures.name: Name
structures.notFound: Structure not found at the expected address.

descriptions.slot_info: Start of RAM: where the active slot's kernel and userland are. Re-read from memory each time.
descriptions.slot_header: Security level and size of the slot's signed payload.
descriptions.kernel_header: Epsilon version and build commit identifier, in the kernel.
descriptions.userland_header: What the kernel knows about the userland: app areas, storage, device name.
descriptions.vector_table: Userland entry points: initial stack, start, text drawing function.
descriptions.storage: The calculator's file buffer in RAM, with its start and end markers.
descriptions.apps: External apps written to flash, re-read from memory.
descriptions.app: What linking did with the application: addresses of code, data and heap.

keys.name: Mapping name
keys.help: Highlighted calculator keys have a binding. Hover one to see which; click one to edit it.
keys.selectHint: Click a calculator key to see and edit its bindings.
keys.notMapped: Nothing is bound to this key.
keys.byPosition: by position (same on AZERTY and QWERTY)
keys.pressAKey: Press the computer key to bind…
keys.addToCombo: Add a key to the combination
keys.keyboardHelp: Each row binds a computer key to one or more calculator keys, pressed together (for example Shift + arrow). The “+” menu adds a key to the combination.
keys.touchHelp: On a touch screen (or with the mouse), a gesture on the calculator's screen presses keys. Each row pairs a gesture, a number of fingers and the keys to press.

gestureInfo.swipe_left: slide the finger to the left (distance below)
gestureInfo.swipe_right: slide the finger to the right

keys.gestureHint: The movement that triggers the rule.
keys.fingersHint: Number of fingers down at the same time for this gesture (1 to 3).
keys.calcKeysHint: The calculator keys pressed together when the gesture is recognized.
keys.heldHint: For a long press: the key stays down as long as the finger stays down, instead of a brief press.
keys.thresholdsHelp: These values tune how sensitive gesture recognition is; they are saved in the .nmk file.
keys.swipeDistanceInfo: Minimum distance the finger must travel to count as a swipe rather than a simple touch.
keys.longPressInfo: How long the finger must stay down, without moving, to count as a long press.
keys.doubleTapInfo: Maximum time between two touches for them to form a double tap.
keys.pressMsInfo: How long the key stays down for a brief gesture (tap, swipe, double tap), so the application has time to see it.

settings.speedHelp: The model sets the real frequency (192 or 540 MHz); “unlimited” runs the app as fast as possible, paced by the 60 frames per second.
settings.help: Each setting is rewritten where the device keeps it (flash headers, name, FCC…): applications see it through system calls or by reading memory.

hints.device_name: Name the user gave the calculator; empty: none.
hints.fcc_id: Shown by the About app and returned by the fcc_id system call.
hints.serial_number: Returned by the serial_number_copy system call.
hints.software_version: Epsilon version written in the kernel header.
hints.expected_userland_version: Userland version the kernel expects: it differs after a partial update.
hints.brightness: In steps of 16: 0, 16, … 240, as on the calculator.
hints.usb_plugged: What the app reads when asking whether USB is plugged in.
hints.exam_mode: Hides external apps: they can no longer be launched.
hints.clearance_level: 0 official, 1 third-party apps installed, 2 third-party userland.
hints.compilation_flags: Value returned by the compilation_flags system call.

settings.autoReloadHint: With the Nwasabi server: when the application, data, mapping, files or state change on disk, the page reloads them by itself. Otherwise a “Reload” button (or Ctrl + R) appears.

keep.label: Keep the files in the browser
keep.help: The calculator's files and the last applications you opened are copied into this browser's data; the files are restored at each launch (the site asks on the first visit); the browser may ask your permission to keep them durably. They are shared by everything that runs on this site, in this browser: remember to erase them on a computer that is not yours.
keep.stored: no files kept | 1 file kept ({size}) | {n} files kept ({size})
keep.notPersistent: persistent storage not granted (the browser may erase it when space runs low)
keep.failed: Could not save: the browser storage is full or blocked.
keep.confirmClear: Erase the files kept in this browser? The current calculator's files are not touched. This cannot be undone.

trace.cpuHelp: The processor is an ARM Cortex-M7. Its registers are small 32-bit memories inside the chip, read at regular intervals (those that just changed are highlighted).

flag.N: N (negative): the last result is negative, its top bit is 1.
flag.Z: Z (zero): the last result is zero, or a comparison found two equal values.
flag.C: C (carry): an addition overflowed, or a subtraction did not borrow; used for unsigned comparisons.
flag.V: V (overflow): the result does not fit in a signed 32-bit integer.
flag.Q: Q (saturation): a saturating instruction reached its limit; the flag stays set until cleared.

trace.svcHelp: The application's calls to the kernel (svc instruction), from most to least frequent ({frames} frames).

regInfo.args: Arguments and result of a function (r0 to r3); a function may overwrite them freely.
regInfo.saved: Local variables: a function must restore them as it found them.
regInfo.r12: Temporary scratch register (IP), freely overwritten by calls.
regInfo.sp: Stack pointer (r13): top of the stack, where local variables and return addresses live.
regInfo.lr: Link register (r14): where to resume when the current function returns.
regInfo.pc: Program counter (r15): address of the instruction being executed.
regInfo.xpsr: Status register: flags N Z C V Q, the Thumb bit and the current exception number.
regInfo.fpscr: Floating-point control and status: rounding mode and error flags.

trace.flagsHelp: Four bits of xpsr sum up the result of the last operation and drive conditional branches; the ones that are set are colored.

svcInfo.3: Tells whether the battery is charging.
svcInfo.18: Reads the pixels of a screen rectangle.
svcInfo.19: Draws a rectangle of pixels on the screen.
svcInfo.20: Fills a rectangle with a single color.
svcInfo.21: Waits for the current frame to end (vertical sync).
svcInfo.22: Copies the text associated with an event.
svcInfo.23: Waits for and returns the next event (key…).
svcInfo.24: Tells whether an event has a defined meaning.
svcInfo.33: Removes and returns the queued keyboard state.
svcInfo.34: Reads the current state of the keys.
svcInfo.49: Waits for a number of milliseconds.
svcInfo.50: Waits for a number of microseconds.
svcInfo.52: Tells whether the USB cable is plugged in.
svcInfo.55: Repeat count of a held key.
svcInfo.129: Grows the heap, the application's dynamic memory.
svcInfo.130: Writes text to the standard output.

keepPrompt.title: Keep your files?
keepPrompt.message: Should Nwasabi keep the calculator's files (your scripts, for example) in this browser, so you find them again on every visit? The browser may ask your permission to keep them durably. They stay on this computer, are shared by everything that runs on this site, and you can erase them or change your mind at any time in the Settings tab.

scan.title: Memory value search
scan.help: This search finds the memory addresses that hold a given value. The first search keeps every matching address; each next search keeps, among them, only those whose new value satisfies the chosen comparison (exact value, changed, increased…). Repeating it after each change of the value in the application isolates the address that holds it. The retained addresses can be added to the list to be read continuously, modified or held at a value.
scan.noApp: Load an application to search its memory.
scan.aligned: Addresses aligned to the type size only (faster, and almost always what you want)
scan.showing: The first {n} results are shown: narrow the search.
scan.truncated: Too many results: the search stopped at {n} addresses.
scan.listHelp: Values are read continuously. Typing a value and pressing Enter writes it to memory, in the format of the address's type; “Hold” keeps writing the value so that it stays unchanged.
scan.listEmpty: The list is empty: add addresses from the results.
scan.badValue: “{text}” is not a valid value for this type ({type}).

quick.title: Quick save
quick.help: One slot in this browser, no file: Ctrl + S saves the emulation state (application, memory, files, processor), Ctrl + O reloads it.
quick.saveHint: Saves the state in this browser (the simulation pauses for a moment).
quick.loadHint: Replaces the emulation with the saved state and resumes it.
